summary: This Makefile orchestrates a Docker-based Joomla development environment. It provides commands to start, stop, and configure the application, managing both the web server and database containers while injecting the current user's ID and group ID into Docker to handle file permissions correctly. The main entry point is the 'start' target, which displays formatted installation details pulled from environment variables.

explanations.1: This loads variables from a .env file so they can be used throughout the Makefile—things like WEB_PORT, DB_USER, etc.
explanations.4: The $$(id -u) and $$(id -g) capture the current user's ID and group ID; these are passed to Docker so containers run with matching permissions and can access files without ownership conflicts.
explanations.7: The leading dash (-) tells Make to ignore errors if this command fails; the @ symbol suppresses printing the command itself before running it.
explanations.16: The 'clear' command wipes the terminal screen to give a clean slate for the startup message.
explanations.17: This uses printf with ANSI escape codes to print colored text—the codes like \033[1;33m control colors (yellow here) and formatting.
explanations.23: This printf formats and aligns output: %-30s reserves 30 characters left-aligned for the label, then prints the variable value in a different color.
explanations.39: This creates the db_data and joomla_data directories if they don't exist, using -p to create parent directories without errors if they're already there.
explanations.40: The --detach flag runs containers in the background, and --build forces a rebuild of images before starting.
